mechanism_narrative: A sustained low level of federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which tends to boost equity markets by reducing borrowing costs and increasing liquidity.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following a low FEDFUNDS period, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate indicates a weakening labor market, which may lead to decreased consumer spending and negative impacts on corporate earnings and equity prices.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 exhibits positive returns in more than 50% of the 60-day periods following an unemployment rate increase above 8%, the hypothesis is invalidated.

mechanism_narrative: Growth in real final sales indicates strong consumer demand, which can lead to increased corporate revenues and positive equity returns.
failure_condition: If real final sales growth is positive but the S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 30% of the subsequent 20-day periods, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in unemployment combined with a decrease in payroll employment suggests a deteriorating labor market, which may negatively impact the S&P 500.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases by 0.5% and PAYEMS decreases
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 40% of the 60-day windows following the trigger conditions, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production suggests strong economic activity, which can lead to higher corporate earnings and positive equity returns.
failure_condition: If industrial production rises but the S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 35% of the subsequent 20-day periods, the hypothesis is invalidated.

mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rates combined with rising consumer prices may lead to decreased consumer spending and negative equity returns.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 45% of the 60-day windows following the trigger conditions, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts indicates strong demand in the housing market, which can lead to increased economic activity and positive equity returns.
failure_condition: If housing starts rise but the S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of the subsequent 5-day periods, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: During a late-cycle expansion, a rising unemployment rate may signal an impending economic slowdown, leading to negative equity returns.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of the 60-day periods following the trigger conditions, the hypothesis is invalidated.
